correctness.rationale: Independent derivation: DLMF 16.11.2/16.11.8 yields the first two 1F2 algebraic residues and an oscillatory remainder o(z^(-2lambda-2)) because mu>lambda+2. Hubbert–Jäger (2.10) plus DLMF 10.22.57 yields a Mellin gamma ratio. Bessel J_nu is exponentially small on z<=nu/2; on z>=nu/2 the transform remainder integrates to o(nu^-2) relative. Exact Mellin ratio and Bernoulli B3 gamma expansion produce Q. Positive factors imply the unique scale epsilon_star and signs. A standalone numerical checker independently confirms transform residues, Bessel integrals, gamma coefficient and generic/tuned circle coefficients. These finite tests do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The focal 2021 arXiv version expressly claimed the all-dimensional first-order asymptotic, and the 2023 journal version proves the precise first order only in odd d; therefore leading coefficient and parity problem are NOT claimed as novel. Neither primary version nor the reviewed 2007 radial/SBF transfer paper states the explicit relative nu^-2 correction or the unique positive scale cancellation. DLMF formulas are used as ingredients but do not give this combined classification. No duplicate with the inspected own ledger or semantically searched published published-finding corpus records was identified; remaining possible unlocated all-order kernel literature is a priority risk.
residual_risks: The first 2021 preprint expressly states the leading asymptotic in even dimensions, contrary to the revised 2023 open-question framing; only the second-order refinement is claimed new.
A specialized all-orders expansion for smooth radial kernels or a parameterized kernel-preconditioner might contain Q implicitly and was not exhaustively located.
The o(nu^-2) remainder is pointwise in fixed parameters and requires mu>lambda+2, not uniform or boundary mu=lambda+2.

value.rationale: The exact next-to-leading term is a motivated refinement of the known Sobolev-equivalence decay law for compactly supported spherical kernels. Its identically zero 1/nu term and unique positive kernel-support scale where the entire 1/nu^2 correction disappears are meaningful structural phenomena: they characterize an exact leading-order spectral-bias calibration for every fixed dimension and smoothness choice in a nontrivial open parameter region. The result is more than an isolated numerical coefficient and directly informs high-degree kernel spectra without overclaiming finite-dimensional optimality.
